spatial_claims.claim: A and B are distinct points on the circumference; M is the midpoint of segment AB (AM = MB), so M lies on segment AB and inside the circle
Line ℓ is perpendicular to AB at M, extending in both directions
O (center) satisfies OA = OB; if O on line AB and outside segment AB, one of OA/OB strictly contains the other, so they are unequal
If O on segment AB and O ≠ M, then O is closer to one endpoint, making OA ≠ OB
O cannot equal A or B because the center is inside the circle; conclusion: O on line AB implies O = M, hence O on ℓ
When O is not on line AB, triangles AMO and BMO have AM = BM, MO common, OA = OB; SSS congruence gives angle AMO = angle BMO
Angles AMO and BMO are adjacent on line AB and equal, so both are right angles
X on ray of ℓ from M on same side of AB as O; angle AMX = right angle (ℓ ⊥ AB) and angle AMO = right angle (Step 4); rays MX and MO must coincide
O lies on ℓ in every case (combining Steps 3 and 5)
ℓ meets the circumference at C and D on opposite sides of O; since O (center) is on ℓ, CD is a diameter
K is the midpoint of CD (CK = KD); if K ≠ O, ordering C,K,O,D gives CO > CK = KD > OD, contradicting CO = OD
K = O, so the constructed midpoint of the diameter is the center

configuration_map: Circle with center O (position unknown initially). A,B on circumference. M = midpoint of AB, on segment AB, inside circle. Line ℓ perpendicular to AB at M. O proven to lie on ℓ in all cases: (1) if O on line AB, betweenness and midpoint uniqueness force O = M which is on ℓ; (2) if O off line AB, SSS congruence makes angles AMO = BMO = right angle, and perpendicular uniqueness forces ray MO onto ℓ. Then C,D = ℓ ∩ circumference on opposite sides of O, making CD a diameter. K = midpoint of CD; one-dimensional betweenness argument on ℓ forces K = O.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The proof's case analysis (O on vs off line AB) correctly handles point positions. The perpendicular uniqueness argument in Step 5 is valid (two rays from M on the same side of AB each making right angles must coincide). The betweenness argument in Step 6 for K = O on line ℓ is sound. No angle decomposition issues arise since all angle reasoning involves right angles from perpendicularity, not problematic interior-point decompositions.
